Fit modular calibration conditional on emulator posterior draws

Source: R/calibration_fit.R
calibration_fit.Rd

Targets one conditional posterior per fixed emulator coefficient set and pools equal numbers of samples. The emulator is not updated by field observations. Gaussian emulator fields are integrated out. By default discrepancy states are also integrated out using a Kalman filter.

Usage

calibration_fit(
  object,
  z,
  U,
  locations = seq_len(object$S),
  backend = "rstan",
  draws = seq_len(object$M),
  chains = 1L,
  iter,
  warmup = iter%/%2L,
  draws_per_emulator = min(200L, chains * (iter - warmup)),
  n0 = 30,
  d0 = 2,
  discount = 1,
  m0 = rep(0, length(locations)),
  M0 = diag(length(locations)),
  seed = 1234L,
  cores = 1L,
  marginal_discrepancy = TRUE,
  keep_predictions = FALSE,
  keep_discrepancy = TRUE,
  control = if (warmup == 0L) list(adapt_engaged = FALSE, stepsize = 0.001, max_treedepth
    = 12L) else list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 12L),
  refresh = 100L,
  checkpoint_dir = NULL,
  cache = TRUE,
  cache_dir = NULL,
  compiled_model = NULL,
  init = "mode",
  mode_starts = 20L,
  parallel_draws = 1L
)

Arguments

object

Prepared emulator from calibration_prepare().

z

Finite time-by-observed-location matrix of field observations.

U

Full-grid symmetric positive-definite discrepancy covariance scale. Correlation matrices are supported, but the diagonal need not equal one. Discrepancy increments have covariance tau2t * U; observation errors retain covariance tau2t * I.

locations

Ordered original-grid indices corresponding to columns of z.

backend

Currently "rstan".

draws

Emulator draw indices to use, without duplicates.

chains, iter, warmup

Number of chains, total iterations per chain, and warmup iterations for each emulator-conditional fit. iter has no default and must be given. For inference use several chains and enough iterations, for example chains = 4, iter = 2000; iter = 1 (with no warmup) is a quick execution check, not inference. chains defaults to one and warmup to floor(iter / 2).

draws_per_emulator

Equal number of retained samples per conditional. Defaults to the smaller of 200 and the available post-warmup samples.

n0, d0

Positive inverse-gamma shape and scale hyperparameters.

discount

Calibration variance discount factor in (0, 1].

m0, M0

Initial discrepancy mean and covariance scale at observed sites.

seed

Nonnegative integer RNG seed, local to the function call.

cores

Positive number of parallel chains. Defaults to one.

marginal_discrepancy

Whether to integrate out discrepancy states.

keep_predictions, keep_discrepancy

Whether to recover and retain latent fields, replicated observations, and discrepancy states.

control

Named list passed to rstan sampling. With zero warmup the defaults disable adaptation and use stepsize = 0.001. With warmup they use adapt_delta = 0.95. Both use max_treedepth = 12.

refresh

Stan progress reporting interval.

checkpoint_dir

Optional directory for completed conditional fits. Each fit is saved as it completes; a fit already saved there with the same data, settings, seed and Stan program is reused instead of refitted, so an interrupted calibration resumes where it stopped.

cache, cache_dir

Whether to reuse compiled models and optional user cache directory. Installed package files are never modified.

compiled_model

Optional compatible compiled Stan model for advanced use.

init

Starting values of the free parameters for every chain. "mode" (the default) runs L-BFGS (rstan::optimizing()) from mode_starts random starts in each conditional fit and starts every chain, slightly jittered, at the optimum with the highest log posterior density, with the precisions of that optimum. Chains started far from the main mode can settle in local modes of negligible posterior mass, which this avoids; the optima found are recorded in diagnostics[[j]]$mode_search. "random" draws each chain's start uniformly within the bounds, reproducibly from seed, so that \(\hat R\) can reveal chains that settle in different modes; "midpoint" starts every chain at the centre of the bounds; or give a numeric vector of parameter values in training-column order (named vectors are matched by name), strictly inside the bounds of the free parameters. Values given for fixed parameters are ignored. Each conditional fit starts afresh; except for "mode", precisions start at n0 / d0.

mode_starts

Number of random starts of the mode search for init = "mode".

parallel_draws

Number of conditional fits (one per emulator draw) run at the same time, in forked processes. Each forked fit runs its chains one after another, so cores is then not used and parallel_draws processes run at once. With a multithreaded BLAS (for example oneMKL or OpenBLAS), start R with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1: forking after the BLAS has used several threads can leave the forked fits hung, and calibration_fit() warns when it detects that setup. Results do not depend on it: every fit draws its random numbers from its own seeds, and rstan's draws do not depend on the number of cores. Forking is unavailable on Windows, where fits run one after another. Defaults to one.

Value

An ordinary serializable list of class spDBL_calibration containing samples, per-conditional diagnostics, settings, and prediction context. No compiled Stan model is stored in the result.

Details

Requires the suggested package rstan and a C++ toolchain on first compilation. One iteration per emulator draw is an execution experiment, not converged posterior inference; its samples stay near init. When the midpoint of the bounds is close to the true value, as in dt_calibration, use init = "random" to check that results do not depend on the start. Missing observations and new time/grid locations are not supported in this initial interface.

See also

calibration_predict(), calibration_validate()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive() && requireNamespace("rstan", quietly = TRUE)
data("dt_calibration")
d <- dt_calibration
em <- emulator_learn(d$training$input, d$training$responses, d$Nx, d$Ny,
                     covariance = "sigma2R", episode_window = 2, nsam = 3,
                     seed = 1)
cal <- calibration_prepare(em, d$lower, d$upper)
fit <- calibration_fit(cal, d$field$z, d$field$U,
                       locations = d$field$locations, draws = 1:2,
                       chains = 1, iter = 200, seed = 1)
summary(fit)
}
